howToRead: One entry per SUBJECT, not per finding. The two corpora file the same subject under different ids, different domains and different wording; `from` records every id on each side that speaks to it.
`carries` = permission to copy the substance across. The authoring agent still writes it against THIS corpus's evidence and re-derives every count.
`retired` = nothing to compare against, or the comparison proved it false. The `why` says which.
`changed` = the subject is real but the previous statement is wrong in a way that matters. The `why` says what changes.
`recheck` = cannot be settled from what exists. Go and look.
Where a comparison report ruled one run wrong, that ruling is not re-argued here. Do not re-argue it either.

Two things make dr1c different and drive most of the `recheck` rows. (1) Both previous runs read screenshots at half the resolution they claimed and read element crops that were often of the wrong control — 31 crops across the two sides matched more than one element and were cut at whichever came first; the manifests now record `matched` per crop. (2) The frontend's permanent-address identification card was never photographed by either run; it is now `fe-animal-identification-permanent-address` on the frontend side, against `dr1-permanent-address-animals` on the prototype side.
Capture facts for dr1c: viewport 1280x1200, deviceScaleFactor 2, so page PNGs are 2560 wide. Any pixel measurement carried over from either run was taken at the wrong scale.

Heads are unchanged from both previous runs: frontend 76a864ba, prototype 491b3926. So a screen-set count that was true then is probably still true, but the frontend side has gained one screen (41, not 40).

subjects.subject: A user importing horses on temporary admission is never asked the port of exit or the exit date on the way through, and the hub's Exit details row reads 'Cannot start yet' and never changes.
subjects.why: dr1's account of the forward path is wrong and the defect is worse than dr1 describes. RUN_STEPS (linear/flow/run.js:22-39) does not include destination country, port of exit or exit date; `kit.nextTarget` (shared/kit.js:96-100) consults `runTarget` first, `nextRunTarget` never returns null (it falls back to hubPath at run.js:50), so `nextInSection` — the mechanism dr1 cites — cannot fire while the opening run is active. `completeOpeningRun` is called only by the hub GET handler (hub/controller.js:155). The row mechanism both runs agree on holds: `rowGatePasses` consults `row.pages[0]` only (flow/navigation.js:25) where `rowEntry` two lines above searches for the first PASSING page, and the exitDetails row's pages[0] is destinationCountryPage (task-rows.js:34-39).
subjects.notes: State it at dr1b's strength, not dr1's. dr1 says the user 'can complete the notification' and has merely lost the return route; in fact `portOfExit` and `exitDate` are both `status: 'mandatory'` for this reason (obligations/sections/import-reason.js:84-113) and `readyForCheckYourAnswers` requires every row fulfilled, so Check and submit stays shut too — the notification cannot be finished by anything the interface tells the user to do. The one route that works is re-opening 'Main reason for importing' from the hub and pressing the unnamed primary button (shared/save-actions.njk:6 carries no `name`, so hubExitTarget returns null and nextInSection walks to Port of exit then Exit date). Nothing signposts it. Also drop dr1b's clause 'every other row on the same page … is a working link' — fe-hub-exit-details-blocked.html has TWO cannot-start-yet rows (Exit details at :183 and Check and submit at :324); dr1's phrasing 'every other startable row' is the correct one. PROVENANCE note: this is the one subject where a dr1b agent saw two dr1 finding FILE NAMES in a grep output, so the two runs both choosing to write about this screen is worth nothing as evidence. The substance was re-derived independently and stands; and on the leg that decides the finding's value the two runs DISAGREE, which contamination could not have produced. temporaryAdmissionHorses is the only reason value that produces shown-but-blocked, and that falls out of obligations/sections/import-reason.js:60-113 alone.

DR1's reveal order is the one dr1b gives.

Also delete dr1b's sentence 'the four gates already encode exactly the right conditions and do not change' — for two of the four fields there is no validation to relocate, because the frontend has none (see the two validation rows below). And do not treat this merge as covering those six subjects: dr1 raised the same merge as one finding AND kept the six, so the merge saved nothing and cost six separately-schedulable rows.

subjects.subject: DR1 fills in the selected country's code as a fixed prefix and asks only for the part after it; the frontend asks the user to type the whole region-of-origin code.

subjects.subject: The frontend refuses to save the origin page until a country of origin is chosen; DR1 lets the user save what they have and shows the task as still to do.

DR1 applies the same pattern on origin — `validateOriginOfImport` checks only the region-code branch and never looks at `countryOfOrigin`, while `hasOriginDetails` (app/routes.js:231-244) returns false without it. The frontend is not consistent with itself either: origin/controller.js:63-67 uses `requiredOneOf` on countryOfOrigin while import-reason/controller.js:25-30 uses plain `oneOf` on reasonForImport, so the frontend already implements DR1's soft-save on one of the two pages.
subjects.notes: REVERSE dr1b's standing instruction. dr1b declined this in inc-082's correction and wrote 'Declining it was right and it should not be raised on a later pass.' The decline reads DR1's silence as a prototype defect, and that reasoning proves too much — run it on `importReason` and DR1's explicitly commented soft save becomes a defect too. Raise it.

subjects.subject: The frontend rejects an internal reference containing a space, hyphen or slash; DR1 imposes no rule on it at all.

DR1: app/routes.js:9240-9244 trims and stores the value, `validateOriginOfImport` never looks at it and `hasOriginDetails` never tests it.
subjects.notes: The cleanest provable miss in the domain: dr1b's inc-082 verification line recites the whole composed rule list including 'a pattern rule on internalReferenceNumber' and quotes DR1's single validation branch in the same paragraph, and neither half became a finding.

subjects.subject: DR1 lets the user import any of twenty-one commodities and 144 species; the frontend offers five commodities and eight species.
subjects.why: The substance is sound on both sides. The band changes: dr1's `needs-backend` ('the catalogue has to come from reference data') is an architectural preference stated as a blocker and nothing in the corpus supports the 'has to'. Both sides are local data modules — `services/commodities/stub.js` and `app/data/commodities.js` — `services/commodities/index.js:1-15` imports the constants directly with no client, `src/config/config.js` has no commodities reference-data entry, the repo's own doc calls commodities a set-owned service ('This vocabulary is not a generic platform contract', sets/live-animals/docs/services.md:5-12), and no live-animals commodity-code validation exists on the backend.
subjects.notes: Band `frontend-work` with dr1b's named pre-flight: confirm the notification payload mapping accepts the new commodity codes; if it does not, this becomes backend work first. Carry dr1b's enumeration, which is the implementation detail dr1 lacks entirely — eight allow-lists at services/commodities/stub.js:50-119, of which EAR_TAG gains Pig, Sheep and Goat and PERMANENT_ADDRESS gains Ferret. Carry dr1b's other real find: DR1's nine per-commodity `certificationPurposeOptions` arrays are DEAD DATA — `getAdditionalAnimalDetailsConfig` (app/routes.js:1187-1198) returns the module-level flat 16-option list required at app/routes.js:15 — so do not port them. Two things to fix in dr1b's text: (a) 'each new commodity needs an entry in every list that applies to it' reads as though PACKAGE_COUNT_COMMODITIES is already done — it is 54 entries long and names goats, pigs, sheep, ferrets and reptiles in IPAFFS format, but it is matched against `entry.commoditySelection` (consignment-details/fields.js:12-13) which only ever holds 'Cow'|'Horse'|'Cat'|'Dog'|'Fish', so those entries can never match; (b) drop the internal tension between 'DR1 has no farmed-fish commodity at all' and 'Ornamental fish three against one'. Do NOT fold the CPH polarity into this row — see the CPH row.

subjects.subject: DR1 refuses to move on until a number of animals is entered for every species; the frontend accepts the field left blank and saves the blank.

The old crops here were ambiguous (`label-consignor` and `label-consignor-or-exporter` each matched two elements on fe-addresses-hub); the claim is settled from the DOM strings, not the crop.

The write endpoints exist: address-book `OperatorController.java` — `@RequestMapping("/organisation/{orgId}/addresses")` at :44, `@PostMapping` at :144, `@PutMapping` at :265, `@DeleteMapping` at :331. What is missing is the frontend client's write path, and that is a recorded ownership DECISION, not a missing capability — services/address-book/index.js:17-19 says 'This service reads and never writes … belongs to the INS frontend, which is the only writer'. dr1 quotes that comment accurately and reads a service-ownership decision as a backend blocker; the INS front-door is another Node frontend, not a backend.
subjects.notes: Carry dr1's richer account of what 'done' means, which dr1b does not have at all: an accepted workspace decision of 19 August that the missing signpost is a deliberate temporary measure, and an explicit 'what the finding does not license is treating the bare picker as a defect to fix next'. dr1's premise verification is also stronger — it searched the whole frontend for every spelling of an add-address route and found only two tests asserting `createAddressHref` is undefined.

subjects.notes: Write the mechanism as both halves. dr1b's names the rule that will still be true once a trader adds a record; dr1's does not. dr1 files this as its own row and dr1b merges it into the picker-scoping row — dr1's split reads better as a decision surface, because the two pages have two different DR1 mechanisms. Band `needs-backend` on both sides.

subjects.subject: DR1 narrows the address list as the user types; the frontend leaves the list alone until Search is pressed and the page reloads.
subjects.why: The claim is sound — `_address-picker.njk:8-12` says in its own comment 'no client JS anywhere', the Search button is `name="action" value="search"` on a POST form, and DR1's filtering is service code the design team wrote (app/assets/javascripts/consignment-address-search.js), not Prototype Kit behaviour. The PREMISE is wrong: dr1b's difference slot says DR1's 'address book holds nine records against the frontend's thirteen'. It holds THIRTY-THREE (`grep -c "type:" app/data/consignment-addresses.js` → 33); nine is the count AFTER the role filter, which is the very filtering dr1b's own scoping finding documents.
subjects.notes: The wrong premise is load-bearing — it is the whole reason dr1b declined to raise the pagination half. From a 33-record book DR1 renders every match with no pagination markup anywhere on the page, so the capture demonstrates the behaviour rather than failing to. dr1's inc-013 and inc-014 both state the 33 correctly.

subjects.notes: dr1b split this off from its live-search finding and DROPPED it on the false nine-versus-thirteen premise; a grep of the whole dr1b backlog for pagination|paging|pager|PAGE_SIZE returns only that one finding. Carry the two consequences dr1b never reaches: PAGE_SIZE = 5 forces the `govukInsetText` restating the choice (_address-picker.njk:97-99), a control that exists only because the chosen row may be on a page the trader is not looking at; and dropping pagination WITHOUT the role scoping would put all thirteen records on one page for every role, a longer list than DR1 ever shows. That sequencing constraint is the reason this row depends on the role-scoping row.

subjects.subject: The two sides offer different places as the port of entry: DR1 searches a UK-wide gazetteer including Northern Ireland and the Crown Dependencies; the frontend searches 78 Great Britain ports and airports and no Northern Ireland location at all.
subjects.why: The subject is real and is the most valuable thing in either run's transport set — dr1 says nothing about list membership anywhere (`grep 'Belfast'` over dr1's backlog returns 0). Two claims must change. (1) The count is 205, not 213: counting quoted strings in `app-airport-search__data` at dr1-arrival-details.html:363 gives 205, and eight entries contain an internal comma ('Broadford, Isle of Skye', 'Kettletoft, Sanday', 'Lochboisdale (Loch Baghasdail), South Uist', 'Millport, Great Cumbrae', 'Pierowall, Westray', 'Rothesay, Isle of Bute', 'Tarbert, Loch Fyne', 'Whitehall Village, Stronsay'), so a comma split gives 213. The 28-airport prefix is right, so the seaport gazetteer is 177, not 185. (2) 'The frontend's 78 read as the border-control-post set' is refuted by the frontend's own copy — fe-port-of-exit.html:16, 'Exit and entry share the same port list' — and by its members (Cambridge Airport, Coventry Airport, Northampton Airport, Nottingham Port, Perth Port, Barking Port, Methil Port, Hythe Port). dr1b contradicts itself: its own origin finding says the 78 are 'most of which cannot handle live animals'.
subjects.notes: Band `disputed` survives, but on the other leg, which is solid: DR1 contradicts itself. dr1-declaration.html:36 scopes responsibility 'to when it enters Great Britain' and dr1-transporter says 'in, to, from or through Great Britain (GB)', while dr1-arrival-details.html:49 offers Belfast, Larne, Warrenpoint, Kilkeel, Londonderry, Coleraine, Kilroot, Ardglass, Jersey, Guernsey and Isle of Man as entry points. The settling question is the authoritative list of entry points a live-animal consignment may be notified against, plus whether NI arrivals are in scope for this service.

subjects.notes: Neither corpus states this. It is the frame that makes the port-of-exit row and the port-of-entry row one decision rather than two, and it is why the frontend's exit hint has to change when the exit list is narrowed.

subjects.subject: Five port names in the frontend's port-of-entry list are malformed or duplicated; DR1 shows each of those places once and spelt correctly.
subjects.why: All five confirmed verbatim in fe-arrival-details.html: 'Teestort (GB TEE)', 'TILBURY (GB TIL)', 'Portsmouth  Port (GB PME)' (doubled space), 'Port of Sheerness (GBSHS)' beside 'Port of Sheerness (GB SHS)', and 'Pembroke Port (GB PED)' beside 'Pembroke Port (GB PEM)'. DR1 holds Teesport - GBTEE, Tilbury - GBTIL and one Sheerness - GBSHS, and no Pembroke or Portsmouth entry.
subjects.notes: One `needs-backend` row for all five, not a three/two split — the list reaches the frontend at runtime (services/ports/client.js fetches `${referenceDataUrl}/ports-of-entry`) and the reference-data service serves it from PortsOfEntryController, which is dr1's own band already. Fix dr1b's TITLE: 'Port of Sheerness twice under the same code' is wrong — the codes are GBSHS and GB SHS, one code with and without a space, which its detail slot has right. dr1b is the only row that lists all five in one place with one destination; dr1 never counts Portsmouth alongside the duplicates.

subjects.subject: DR1's duplicated port names justify treating the frontend's duplicates as possibly intended.
subjects.why: The comparison disproved it. dr1 bands the duplicates `disputed` because DR1's catalogue repeats eight names — Aberdeen, Bristol, Cardiff, Dundee, Glasgow, Inverness, Manchester, Southampton. All eight are real but they are not the same phenomenon: each DR1 pair is an airport and a seaport of the same city under different code systems (Aberdeen - ABZ IATA against Aberdeen - GBABD UN/LOCODE) — two facilities, two records, correctly. The frontend's GBSHS / GB SHS pair is one code with and without a space, which dr1 itself concedes 'is a data defect on its own terms'. The frontend's own list also disambiguates same-city facilities by NAME — Aberdeen Airport (GB DYC) against Aberdeen Harbour (GB ABD), Port of Grimsby against Grimsby and Immingham Port, three separately named Dover entries.
subjects.notes: dr1 then routes the conceded defect out of the backlog ('belongs in a reference-data ticket rather than in this backlog'), which leaves it with nowhere to go. Do not carry the dispute, and do not route the defect out — fold it into the single needs-backend row above.

subjects.subject: DR1 puts no limit on how many countries a consignment travels through.

Remove a country to add another.' at :210, and `updateCountryLimitState` at :164-174 disabling both the input and the search button once twelve are added. The rule lives in the client script that builds the control. Strike this finding; the smaller true subject is the next row.

subjects.subject: DR1 says a commercial transporter can only be one from Northern Ireland and holds its add form to it, while its own directory offers four commercial transporters from Romania, Ireland, Denmark and Portugal; the frontend states no such restriction anywhere.

The frontend hints Commercial as 'A business approved to transport animals — you will choose one from a list' and says nothing about where a transporter may be based, anywhere on the page.
subjects.notes: dr1b declined to file on the ground that the frontend 'carries the same mixture under the same guidance'. The MIXTURE is shared (fe-transporter-commercial offers a Swiss and a Belgian record); the GUIDANCE is not. Band `disputed` — the requirements side contradicts itself, which is what the band is for, and dr1b banded two other findings `disputed` on exactly that reasoning. The rule to apply generally, since this recurs: where the requirements side asserts a rule and its own data breaks it, FILE IT banded `disputed`; file nothing only when there is genuinely no observable difference between the two sides AND no decision is owed. The failure mode of suppression is not a missing row — it is an authoring agent silently ruling that the frontend's current behaviour is correct, with nobody seeing the ruling. Ask both questions dr1 asks: whether an approved commercial transporter may be based outside Northern Ireland, and whether the two records already on the frontend's list may legitimately be there. The second is live today whether or not the add page is ever built.

subjects.subject: DR1 accepts document files up to 50MB; the frontend refuses anything over 10 MB.
subjects.why: Band is `frontend-work` — dr1b's conclusion is right and dr1's `needs-backend` is wrong — but BOTH runs' mechanisms are wrong and dr1b's is wrong in a way that would mislead. dr1b says 'the backend takes its per-upload ceiling from whatever the frontend sends it' and 'the backend is currently being told 10 MB by the very constant this finding changes'. The frontend does put maxFileSize in the initiate body (documents/handlers/reads/download.js:36 into services/document-uploads/real.js:26,38) but the backend's `DocumentUploadRequest.java` declares exactly three components — documentType, documentReference, dateOfIssue — and nothing in src/main overrides Jackson's FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES, so the field is silently discarded. The backend sends its own configured value: DocumentService.java:93 passes `cdpConfig.uploader().maxFileSize()`, and application.yml:45 is `max-file-size: ${CDP_UPLOADER_MAX_FILE_SIZE:52428800}` = 50 MiB, with spring.servlet.multipart at 50MB/51MB (application.yml:29-30).
subjects.notes: So there is nothing on the backend to change and nothing to land first, which is what `frontend-work` means — the band survives more strongly than either run argued. dr1's stated reason (a CDP nginx ingress cap that 'rejects a larger body before the application sees it') is not a dependency to schedule behind: the contract defines needs-backend as 'an API, contract or persistence change has to land first' and an ingress cap is none of the three, and the cap has no corroboration in the corpus beyond two prose comments (documents/upload-config.js:40-41 and the tests repo's resources/file-upload/constants.ts:4-8) — no chart, no manifest, no ingress annotation, no environment variable. Keep it as a pre-flight question for the platform team, in the same piece of work. State the work correctly: one frontend constant, MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB, feeds the hint bullet, data-max-file-size, the hapi maxBytes, the server-side guard and the oversize message.

subjects.subject: The frontend sends a maxFileSize and mimeTypes pair in the upload-initiate body that the backend's request contract does not accept.

Flagged in comparison/documents.md §1 as something neither run recorded and somebody should know.
subjects.notes: NOT a parity difference — it is a live dead-field mismatch between two of our own services, found while settling the file-size band. Record it here so it is not lost, but raise it as its own ticket rather than as a finding in the parity report.
